articles.title: KBRA Chief Strategist Projects if 10-Year Treasury Yield at 5% is ‘Here to Stay’
articles.description: In this NYSE Live interview, Van Hesser, Chief Strategist at KBRA, discusses the factors driving Treasury market volatility, the outlook for Federal Reserve policy, and why fixed income may once again offer compelling opportunities for investors. Hesser begins by examining the recent shifts in investor sentiment that have influenced bond markets. Rising yields, economic uncertainty, inflation concerns, and changing expectations surrounding growth have all contributed to increased volatility across fixed-income markets. A significant portion of the discussion focuses on Treasury yields and what current levels may signal about the broader economy. Hesser explains how movements in the U.S. Treasury market reflect investor expectations regarding growth, inflation, monetary policy, and overall market risk. The interview also explores the impact of artificial intelligence investment trends on financial markets. As investors evaluate the long-term economics of large-scale AI infrastructure spending, questions around growth and capital allocation continue to influence both equity and bond market performance. Another major theme is monetary policy. Hesser discusses how the Federal Reserve may approach interest rates moving forward and examines the relationship between policy decisions, inflation management, and economic growth. The conversation further examines the implications of higher yields for consumers and businesses. Areas such as housing, mortgages, auto loans, and corporate borrowing costs remain highly sensitive to changes in interest rates, making Treasury movements important far beyond financial markets. The interview also highlights the changing opportunity set within fixed income. After years of historically low rates, investors can once again access higher yields that may provide attractive income potential while helping diversify portfolios. Another key topic is portfolio allocation. Hesser notes that higher bond yields may increase the appeal of balanced investment strategies as investors seek ways to manage risk while maintaining exposure to growth opportunities. Additionally, the discussion explores the role of fixed income in a diversified portfolio and why current market conditions may present opportunities for long-term investors willing to rebalance across asset classes. Looking ahead, Hesser expects markets to remain focused on inflation, economic growth, policy decisions, and interest-rate trends as investors assess opportunities across both bonds and equities. Throughout the discussion, Hesser shares perspectives on Treasury markets, fixed income, Federal Reserve policy, inflation, economic growth, interest rates, portfolio construction, diversification, asset allocation, and long-term investing. Disclaimer: Informational content only. NYSE does not endorse or recommend investments, strategies, companies, products, or services discussed.
